question: HPV types 16 and 18 together account for approximately 70% of invasive cervical cancers worldwide.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect — this statement is true. HPV 16 and 18 account for approximately 70% of cervical cancers. The E6 and E7 oncoproteins of these types degrade p53 and pRb, respectively, driving carcinogenesis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. HPV 16 (responsible for the majority) and HPV 18 are the dominant high-risk types, together causing about 70% of cervical cancers. Both are covered by the bivalent, quadrivalent, and nonavalent vaccines.
